faq.q: Which formats can it convert between?
faq.a: It converts to JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF and BMP, and reads any image your browser can display. On load it tests whether your browser can actually encode WebP and AVIF and shows a warning if the chosen format isn't supported, so you won't get a silent empty file.

faq.q: What happens to transparency when I convert a PNG to JPEG?
faq.a: JPEG and BMP can't store transparency, so when you pick one of those a 'Background for transparency' colour picker appears (default white). Transparent pixels are composited onto that colour before encoding, which prevents the common black-box-around-the-logo surprise. For PNG, WebP and AVIF output, transparency is preserved.

faq.q: Can I resize or hit a target file size during conversion?
faq.a: Yes. Resize mode offers 'Max width/height' (scales down to fit, preserving ratio) or 'Scale %'. For lossy formats (JPEG/WebP/AVIF) you can set a Target size in KB, which the tool meets with an ~8-iteration binary search on quality; otherwise you control the quality slider directly (default 92%).

faq.q: Does converting remove EXIF metadata like GPS?
faq.a: Yes — because conversion re-encodes through a canvas, EXIF metadata is stripped by default, so location and camera data don't carry into the output. The tool's own notes caution that format conversion alone isn't a reliable way to strip metadata in general, but this canvas-based converter does drop it. You can batch-convert and download all as a ZIP.
